episodes: Ep 239: Tiny crystals in Andean volcanic rocks share a chemical signature tied to hot magma intrusions that destabilize shallow reservoirs before eruptions.
Ep 238: Brain imaging across 57 studies ties multiple sleep disorders to smaller thalamus volume.
Ep 237: Researchers have mapped how a single metabolite shields its own consuming enzyme from degradation signals in tryptophan metabolism.
Ep 236: A Neurology study linked greater lifetime estrogen exposure to lower cerebrovascular pathology in women.
Ep 235: University of Sydney researchers traced AI unpredictability to fractal "riddled basins" in neural network training landscapes.
Ep 234: Researchers mapped 300-plus 3D genome structures showing lab-grown neurons retain embryonic features unlike adult brain cells.
Ep 233: New modeling shows U.S. structural fire losses could nearly triple by 2060 without added protections or climate action.
Ep 232: AI cloud lab uses robots and models to compress protein engineering from years to days.
Ep 231: Researchers identified claudin-4 as the receptor that lets a common gut bacterium toxin damage colon cells and promote tumors.
Ep 230: Spatial transcriptomics reveals how neighboring tissues send WNT and BMP signals that steer early gonadal cell fate in human embryos.
Ep 229: Boosting fibroblast growth factor 13 from astrocytes slows aging throughout the bodies of mice.
Ep 228: Brainstem cells limit dangerous blood pressure swings even when average readings stay normal.
Ep 227: A daily inulin fiber supplement reduced knee osteoarthritis pain and improved grip strength by shifting gut bacteria and raising GLP-1 levels.
Ep 226: Collaborative study shows drought-avoiding desert plants fared better than drought-tolerating ones during extreme heat at Uluru.
Ep 225: A liquid painted on teeth stops cavities in young children without drilling or anesthesia.
Ep 224: Long-read nanopore sequencing uncovers hidden DNA rearrangements that drive cancer in cases missed by standard short-read methods.
Ep 223: Genetic conflicts between viruses and hosts shape rapid evolution across species.
Ep 222: Rural Argentinian communities slept 35 minutes less per night once electricity arrived.
Ep 221: A muscle substance released in response to cold temperatures delayed aging markers in worms.
Ep 220: Computational models show high-conductance potassium channels evolved to stabilize spike timing by easing calcium competition in neurons.
Ep 219: A nanoscale platform now tracks single proteins moving inside living neurons in real time.
Ep 218: Daily weather swings accelerate glacier melt more than monthly averages had indicated.
Ep 217: Archaeologists have dated the world's oldest known shipwreck to 2700–2400 B.C. from pottery cargo found off Turkey.
Ep 216: Naming a single chicken and describing its habits reduces how often preschoolers select poultry for their meals.
Ep 215: Researchers mapped PFAS across 300 Finger Lakes water bodies and found most concentrations remain low despite widespread presence.
Ep 211: Genome editing now maps every cell division from early embryo to organ formation in mammals.
Ep 204: A protein known as the glue holding cells together also helps epithelial cells swallow dead neighbors in zebrafish and mouse embryos.
Ep 201: Cosmic ray muons reveal electrical fields in thunderstorms far stronger than direct measurements ever captured.
Ep 200: Astronauts show higher hip fracture rates after spaceflights longer than ninety days than after shorter missions.
Ep 199: Exercise slowed epigenetic aging in a randomized trial of breast cancer survivors.
Ep 198: Young hearts age rapidly when placed in older bodies while older hearts rejuvenate in young recipients.
Ep 197: Adult retinas in dogs rewired themselves after single-dose gene therapy, rebuilding damaged connections and recovering vision.
Ep 196: A new analysis of eight major randomized trials shows mammograms lead to far less breast cancer overdiagnosis than earlier estimates suggested.
Ep 195: A polygenic risk score doubled the detection of women under fifty who would develop breast cancer when added to standard clinical models.
Ep 194: Worms given magnetotactic bacteria lived forty three percent longer than controls in a new study.
Ep 193: More time in REM sleep correlates with lower risk for eighty three separate diseases in a study of over ninety five thousand people.
Ep 192: Livestock grazing increases soil carbon storage in subarctic grasslands rather than reducing it.
Ep 191: Blood tests may detect breast and prostate cancer up to eight years before diagnosis through DNA methylation patterns.
Ep 190: An AI model decoded chest X-rays from 3.67 million people and predicted multiple cancers at least one year before diagnosis.
Ep 189: A substack review outlines major gaps in how wearable heart rate metrics support clinical decisions.
Ep 188: Multiomic analysis shows regular exercise produces a distinct immune signature across RNA, epigenetics, metabolites and lipids.
Ep 187: A study of over ninety five thousand people links more REM sleep to lower risk of eighty three diseases.
Ep 186: A randomized trial finds five-year colonoscopy intervals after polyp removal match three-year results for colorectal cancer prevention.
Ep 185: Diet shifts lowered biological age markers in older adults after four weeks.
Ep 184: A gene therapy approach reaches genomic sites inaccessible to CRISPR editing.
Ep 183: A new review outlines how sarcopenia research is shifting from lifestyle prevention toward targeted molecular treatments.
Ep 182: Ancient rocks from Western Australia show water reached deep inside Earth more than three billion years ago.
Ep 181: Long-lived bats combine strong immune defenses with unusual damaged-cell clearance that may guide human aging research.
Ep 180: A 2014 case series found that nine of ten patients with cognitive impairment improved after a personalized metabolic and lifestyle program.
Ep 179: A genomics study links heart disease risk to spleen features through an unexpected axis.
Ep 178: Faster walking pace links to lower cardiovascular and all-cause mortality in large UK Biobank cohort.
Ep 177: Large prospective study of over 500,000 people links borderline anemia to higher all-cause mortality.
Ep 176: Advanced optical imaging now maps metabolic activity inside individual immune cells drawn from routine blood samples.
Ep 175: Archaeologists uncovered 80,000-year-old projectile points in Uzbekistan that match later European designs.
Ep 174: UC San Diego researchers showed a cellular enzyme can read an eight-letter genetic code, expanding beyond life's standard four bases.
Ep 173: Far-ultraviolet light is being tested to curb bird flu spread in poultry without mass culling.
Ep 172: University of Sydney researchers created a biodegradable nanobone scaffold that lets the body recruit its own cells to regrow jawbone without donor grafts.
Ep 171: A 10-year study of nearly 10,000 older women ties drinking more than five cups of coffee daily to lower hip bone density while moderate tea intake links to slightly higher density.
Ep 170: Post-mortem tissue analysis from nearly 1000 donors shows human aging accelerates in two distinct periods during the early 30s and 50s.
Ep 169: Ovarian aging markers now show potential to forecast later disease risk and overall lifespan.
Ep 168: Tuberculosis bacteria generate antibiotic-resistance mutations while drying in air after leaving an infected host.
Ep 167: Experimental eye drops restored light perception and visually guided behavior in blind mice without gene therapy or implants.
Ep 166: Self-contracting muscle implants in mice deliver exercise-like anti-aging effects without movement.
Ep 165: Technion researchers found evolution favors flatter paths when multiple routes offer equal fitness.
Ep 164: Ancient DNA confirms cacao reached eastern North America by the 11th century.
Ep 163: A University of Alberta team is examining whether mechanisms from hibernating snails could protect human hearts under stress.
Ep 162: A review of 51 longevity studies pinpoints which biomarkers shift most consistently under different interventions.
Ep 161: Human cells break down shared proteins more slowly than mouse cells, contributing to longer developmental timelines across species.
Ep 160: Older adults with mild cognitive impairment scored 13% higher on cognitive tests after taking at least 5,000 IU of vitamin D daily.
Ep 159: Tampere researchers created a vitamin B2 hydrogel that crosslinks with blue light under cell-friendly conditions for tissue models.
Ep 158: A new study shows natural forest regrowth delivers carbon and biodiversity gains at up to 96 percent lower cost than tree planting.
Ep 157: Specialized neurons in the mouse hypothalamus drive sleep pressure after prolonged wakefulness through a defined circuit.
Ep 156: A catalog of chemical marks on DNA reveals how cells with identical genomes produce distinct identities and functions.
Ep 155: Tissue-resident T cells sense physical touch, not just chemical signals, McGill work finds
Ep 154: Flightless beetles on Japan's largest island show adaptive divergence within a single landmass.
Ep 153: A stress hormone actively restores myelin sheaths after brain injury in new findings that reframe its role.
Ep 152: Sleep patterns emerge as a predictive data source for disease risk in new analysis.
Ep 151: Investigation questions earlier claims of protective gene variants against Alzheimer's disease.
Ep 150: A new analysis of global data shows apparent slowdowns in scientific disruption were artifacts of measurement methods rather than genuine declines.
Ep 149: Waist-to-hip ratio flags cardiovascular risks that BMI overlooks in large analysis.
Ep 148: Machine learning from drone images maps forest soil fungal diversity without extensive ground sampling.
Ep 147: Prevention of type 2 diabetes should target prediabetes remission rather than waiting for established dysglycemia.
Ep 146: An artificial synapse detected early prostate cancer with perfect accuracy in a blind test of 105 patients by reading DNA markers.
Ep 145: A year of moderate aerobic exercise enlarged the hippocampus by 2 percent in older adults, offsetting typical annual shrinkage.
Ep 144: Generative AI has designed complete viral genomes for the first time, reported in Science.
Ep 143: Rare FNIP gene variants tied to less abdominal fat, greater muscle mass, and sharply lower cardiometabolic disease risk.
Ep 142: A new Ice Age toad species was identified from fossils at La Brea Tar Pits, the first such amphibian discovery in North America in decades.
Ep 141: Human brain treats prior higher body weight as new baseline, triggering stronger hunger after loss.
Ep 140: A study of more than 10 million siblings links birth order to risks for multiple diseases.
Ep 139: Fluorescent probes now let researchers map water-transporting xylem in living plants with greater speed and specificity than older dyes.
Ep 138: A new genetic tool maps how cells choose which of their 20,000 genes to activate at any moment.
Ep 137: Routine clinical brain scans from millions of patients can train AI models that reach specialist-level diagnostic accuracy.
Ep 136: Nanoplastics reach the neonatal mouse brain and form distinct spatial patterns visible in 3D.
Ep 135: A mathematical shape known for tiling puzzles now shows unexpected properties that could twist light into chiral patterns.
Ep 134: Simulations show water's local asymmetry drives proton hopping through clusters of six molecules rather than free drift.
Ep 133: Virtual reality experiments show how artificial light at night changes how coral reef fish react to predators.
Ep 132: US researchers mapped how a rare longevity gene shields the brain from Alzheimer's pathology.
Ep 131: Genomic variants shape engineered T-cell safety and a mouse study shows lifelong valine restriction extends lifespan.
Ep 130: Single-cell mapping shows human hippocampal aging proceeds in distinct non-linear stages with microglia replacement by blood-derived cells.
Ep 129: A Nature study maps the heart's independent neural network that modulates stress responses.
Ep 128: US data show the largest national gap between life expectancy and healthspan at 14 years.
Ep 127: Phase 1 trial finds iPSC-derived neural progenitors safe in subacute spinal cord injury over 2–4 years of follow-up.
Ep 126: AI analysis shows climate shifts drove repeated bursts of bird evolution across Earth's history.
Ep 125: Fossils reveal a previously unknown marsupial order that persisted in Australia for 35 million years.
Ep 124: South African genomics projects now direct 10% of budgets to community-chosen benefits through local decision-making.
Ep 123: A new lab study shows many sweeteners alter gut bacteria growth, with some combinations sharply reducing diversity.
Ep 122: A preprint shows amino acids can form replicating peptides and cell-like structures without nucleic acids or lipids.
Ep 121: Biodiversity delivers the largest productivity gains to drier grasslands precisely during extreme drought.
Ep 120: A newly mapped retinal "commander" cell coordinates separate visual pathways to detect faint details.
Ep 119: A superconducting circuit now hosts the first cyclic quantum heat engine, opening routes to larger quantum systems.
Ep 118: Columbia researchers link serotonin signaling to faster progression of degenerative mitral valve disease in patients carrying a specific genetic variant.
Ep 117: A plastic bottle cap recovered near Japan carried 307 marine organisms, including a worm species new to those waters.
Ep 116: Modified low-protein Mediterranean diet helped mice eat more while losing fat and reducing frailty.
Ep 115: A silicon chip uses electricity and enzymes to write dozens of DNA sequences at once.
Ep 114: Creatine energizes dendritic cells to strengthen an immune pathway against tumors.
Ep 113: A prospective study of 73 adults links subtle heart changes to grey matter damage and memory issues even without heart failure.
Ep 112: A blood test measuring apoB particles may prevent more heart attacks than standard LDL cholesterol screening while staying cost-effective.
Ep 111: Researchers mapped a brain circuit that couples deep sleep to growth hormone release and metabolic regulation.
Ep 110: Intermittent fasting in an 8-hour window raised median lifespan 12% in male mice.
Ep 109: UCLA researchers identified a protein that slows muscle repair in older stem cells while also extending their survival under aging stress.
Ep 108: A new biosensor now tracks a rare lipid that clusters in membrane hotspots during cell stress.
Ep 107: Blood circular RNA panel outperforms pTau217 and amyloid-PET for predicting Alzheimer’s progression.
Ep 106: A brain protein may let toxic tau spread between neurons in Alzheimer’s.
Ep 105: Plasma protein patterns now flag organ-specific risks for dementia, heart disease, and several cancers years ahead.
Ep 104: The week's biggest developments, pulled together — what actually moved, why it matters, and what to watch next.
Ep 103: A solid-state material converts visible sunlight into higher-energy ultraviolet light for potential purification and manufacturing uses.
Ep 102: Sea anemones use a protein that reverses the usual role of a human immune component to fight viruses.
